guide.what: Connectors (conectores or marcadores del discurso) are words and phrases like "además", "sin embargo" or "por eso" that link one idea to the next and show how they relate: adding, contrasting, giving a cause or a result, giving an example, or concluding.

rules.t: Connectors are part of your DELE grade
rules.d: In the writing and speaking tests, examiners grade "coherence and cohesion": how well your ideas flow. A clear, varied set of connectors is one of the fastest ways to move up a band, especially from B1 to B2.
rules.ex: Me gusta la idea. Sin embargo, creo que es muy cara. Por eso, propongo otra opción.
rules.exEn: I like the idea. However, I think it's very expensive. That's why I suggest another option.

rules.t: Put a comma after a connector at the start
rules.d: Most connectors at the start of a sentence take a comma after them. In the middle, put commas around them, or a semicolon before and a comma after. "Porque", "que" and "aunque" in the middle usually need no comma after.
rules.ex: El plan es bueno; sin embargo, falta dinero.
rules.exEn: The plan is good; however, there's no money.

rules.t: Choose the register: formal vs informal pairs
rules.d: Many connectors have a spoken and a formal partner. In a formal letter or essay, use the formal one: pero → no obstante; por eso → por consiguiente; o sea → es decir; además → asimismo; entonces → por lo tanto; bueno/pues → (leave out in writing).
rules.ex: Hablado: "Es caro, o sea, no lo voy a comprar." Escrito: "Es caro; es decir, no es accesible."
rules.exEn: Spoken: "It's expensive, I mean, I won't buy it." Written: "It's expensive; that is, it isn't affordable."

rules.d: Using "pero" or "también" five times in one text looks like A2. Rotate synonyms: for contrast use sin embargo, no obstante, en cambio, aun así; for adding use además, asimismo, es más, incluso; for results use por eso, por lo tanto, por consiguiente.
rules.ex: Además, es barato. Asimismo, está bien ubicado. Es más, tiene parqueo.
rules.exEn: Besides, it's cheap. Likewise, it's well located. What's more, it has parking.

rules.d: Introduction: "Hoy en día…", "En mi opinión…". Arguments: "En primer lugar…", "Además…", "Por un lado… por otro lado…", "Por ejemplo…". Counterargument: "Sin embargo…", "Si bien…", "Ahora bien…", "Aun así…". Conclusion: "En conclusión…", "En definitiva…", "Por todo ello…".
rules.ex: En primer lugar, ahorra tiempo. Sin embargo, aísla a la gente. En conclusión, es útil con límites.
rules.exEn: Firstly, it saves time. However, it isolates people. In conclusion, it's useful with limits.

rules.t: In the oral test, fillers buy you time
rules.d: "Bueno", "pues", "a ver", "este…" and "o sea" let you think without awkward silence and sound natural. Use them at the start of an answer, but don't fill every sentence with them, and never write them in the essay.
rules.ex: A ver, bueno, pues yo creo que la foto muestra una familia en la playa.
rules.exEn: Let's see, well, I think the photo shows a family at the beach.

rules.d: "De ahí que" always takes the subjunctive. "Aunque" takes subjunctive when the fact is unknown or not important. "De modo que" and "de manera que" take subjunctive when they mean purpose (so that).
rules.ex: Los precios subieron; de ahí que la gente compre menos.
rules.exEn: Prices went up; hence people buy less.

rules.d: "Actualmente" means "currently", not "actually" (use "en realidad" or "de hecho"). "Eventualmente" means "possibly / occasionally", not "eventually" (use "al final" or "con el tiempo").
rules.ex: Parece fácil, pero en realidad es bastante difícil.
rules.exEn: It looks easy, but actually it's quite hard.

mistakes.wrong: Sin embargo el plan es bueno.
mistakes.right: Sin embargo, el plan es bueno.
mistakes.why: Put a comma after a connector at the start of a sentence.

mistakes.wrong: Actualmente, no me gusta el café. (meaning "actually")
mistakes.right: En realidad, no me gusta el café.

mistakes.why: To give the reason first, start with "como" (or "ya que"), not "porque".

mistakes.wrong: O sea, el estudio demuestra que… (in a formal essay)
mistakes.right: Es decir, el estudio demuestra que…
mistakes.why: "O sea" is spoken; use "es decir" in formal writing.

mistakes.wrong: Los precios suben; de ahí que la gente compra menos.
mistakes.right: Los precios suben; de ahí que la gente compre menos.
mistakes.why: "De ahí que" always takes the subjunctive.

items.use: The basic contrast word for speech and writing. Put a comma before it: "Es caro, pero es bueno." In a formal essay, swap some for "sin embargo" or "no obstante".
items.ex: El apartamento es pequeño, pero está muy bien ubicado.
items.exEn: The apartment is small, but it's very well located.

items.use: Very common in speech to draw a result or move the story on. Fine in emails; in an essay, "por lo tanto" sounds stronger.
items.ex: No había buses a esa hora, entonces pedimos un taxi.
items.exEn: There were no buses at that time, so we got a taxi.
items.latam: In Panama and much of Latin America "entonces" is the everyday "so"; Spain uses "así que" a bit more.

items.use: Gives the reason after the main idea, usually with no comma. Don't start a written sentence with it; use "como" or "ya que" at the start instead.
items.ex: Llegué tarde al trabajo porque había mucho tráfico en la Transístmica.
items.exEn: I got to work late because there was a lot of traffic on the Transístmica.

items.en: well, OK (to start or buy time)
items.use: Spoken filler to start an answer, accept something or change direction. Great at the start of the oral monologue; never use it in a formal essay.
items.ex: Bueno, para empezar, les voy a hablar de mi barrio.
items.exEn: Well, to start, I'm going to tell you about my neighborhood.

items.use: Spoken marker to start a reply or draw a conclusion: "Pues, no sé." Natural in the speaking test; avoid it in formal writing.
items.ex: ¿No te gusta el plan? Pues propón otra cosa.
items.exEn: You don't like the plan? Well, suggest something else.

items.use: Spoken way to explain what you just said. Use it in conversation; in writing, change it to "es decir".
items.ex: Salgo a las cinco, o sea, puedo llegar a las seis.
items.exEn: I get out at five, I mean, I can be there at six.

items.use: Adds a similar idea; it can go before the verb or at the end. For negative ideas use "tampoco", not "también no".
items.ex: Mi hermana habla inglés y también entiende un poco de francés.
items.exEn: My sister speaks English and also understands a little French.

items.use: Adds a new, often stronger, point. At the start of a sentence put a comma after it: "Además, …". Works in emails, essays and the oral test.
items.ex: El trabajo me queda cerca. Además, el horario es flexible.
items.exEn: The job is close to home. Besides, the hours are flexible.

items.use: Joins a result to the cause, with a comma before it. Neutral: good in emails and speaking; in essays vary it with "por lo tanto".
items.ex: Mañana tengo examen, así que hoy no salgo.
items.exEn: I have an exam tomorrow, so I'm not going out today.

items.use: Points back to the reason you just gave. Very common and neutral. The formal pair is "por consiguiente" or "por ello".
items.ex: Me encanta cocinar; por eso casi nunca como en restaurantes.
items.exEn: I love cooking; that's why I almost never eat at restaurants.

items.use: Introduces a concrete example. Use commas around it when it's in the middle. Every DELE opinion essay should have at least one.
items.ex: Hay muchas formas de ahorrar; por ejemplo, llevar almuerzo al trabajo.
items.exEn: There are many ways to save; for example, taking lunch to work.

items.en: it's just that, the thing is
items.use: Spoken way to give an excuse or explanation. Common in the role-play task; too informal for essays.
items.ex: No puedo ir a la fiesta. Es que tengo que trabajar el sábado.
items.exEn: I can't go to the party. The thing is, I have to work Saturday.

items.use: Spoken agreement or to show something is obvious. Good for reacting in the conversation task; in writing use "evidentemente".
items.ex: —¿Me ayudas con la mudanza? —Claro, ¿a qué hora llego?
items.exEn: "Will you help me move?" "Sure, what time should I come?"

items.use: Introduces a sincere opinion, often "la verdad es que…". Natural in speech and informal emails; too chatty for a formal essay.
items.ex: La verdad, el curso fue más difícil de lo que pensaba.
items.exEn: To be honest, the course was harder than I expected.

items.use: Orders steps in a story or process, like "después". Good for narrating in emails and monologues.
items.ex: Primero fuimos al Casco Viejo y luego cenamos en la Cinta Costera.
items.exEn: First we went to Casco Viejo and then had dinner on the Cinta Costera.
items.latam: In Spain "luego" also often means "later" ("hasta luego"); both uses are understood everywhere.

items.use: Orders events in time. Alone it means "afterwards"; before a noun or verb it needs "de": "después de comer".
items.ex: Terminé el informe. Después, se lo mandé a mi jefa.
items.exEn: I finished the report. Afterwards, I sent it to my boss.

items.use: Starts a list of steps or reasons. Simple and clear in emails and speaking; in a formal essay prefer "en primer lugar".
items.ex: Primero, hay que llenar el formulario; después, pagar en caja.
items.exEn: First, you have to fill out the form; then, pay at the counter.

items.use: Tells how a story or situation ended. Don't confuse it with "finalmente" in lists; "al final" is about the outcome.
items.ex: Queríamos ir a la playa, pero al final nos quedamos en casa.
items.exEn: We wanted to go to the beach, but in the end we stayed home.

items.use: Spoken filler to think or organize your answer. Perfect when the examiner asks a question and you need a second. Never in writing.
items.ex: A ver, creo que la mejor opción es la segunda foto.
items.exEn: Let's see, I think the best option is the second photo.

items.use: Spoken marker to introduce an explanation or suggestion to a friend. Informal; use "mire" with "usted".
items.ex: Mira, si no tienes tiempo, yo te ayudo con eso.
items.exEn: Look, if you don't have time, I'll help you with that.

items.use: Admits a point but keeps your main idea. With a fact use indicative; with something uncertain use subjunctive ("aunque llueva"). Excellent in essays.
items.ex: Aunque el carro es viejo, todavía funciona muy bien.
items.exEn: Although the car is old, it still works very well.

items.use: Gives a known reason at the START of the sentence, then a comma. Don't use "porque" there. Good in emails and essays.
items.ex: Como estaba lloviendo, decidimos ver una película en casa.
items.exEn: Since it was raining, we decided to watch a movie at home.

items.use: Corrects a wrong idea or shows the true situation. Not "actualmente" (= currently), a classic false friend.
items.ex: Parece un barrio tranquilo, pero en realidad hay mucho ruido de noche.
items.exEn: It looks like a quiet neighborhood, but actually it's very noisy at night.

items.use: Adds a fact that proves or strengthens what you said. Comma after it. Very useful in essays and monologues to back up an opinion.
items.ex: El reciclaje funciona. De hecho, mi edificio ya separa la basura.
items.exEn: Recycling works. In fact, my building already separates the garbage.

items.use: Informal "anyway / still" in Latin American speech. Fine in conversation; in writing use "de todas formas" or "aun así".
items.ex: No me invitaron, pero igual voy a pasar a saludar.
items.exEn: They didn't invite me, but I'm going to stop by anyway.
items.latam: Very common in Panama and the rest of Latin America in this sense; in Spain it more often means "maybe".

items.use: Highlights the most important item. No comma needed in the middle of a sentence. Great in essays to point at your strongest reason.
items.ex: Me gusta vivir aquí, sobre todo por la gente.
items.exEn: I like living here, above all because of the people.

items.use: Adds a surprising or extreme case: "incluso los domingos". Neutral; works in all DELE tasks.
items.ex: El restaurante estaba lleno; incluso había gente esperando afuera.
items.exEn: The restaurant was full; there were even people waiting outside.

items.use: Strong agreement or something obvious. Polite and neutral; good for replying in emails and conversation.
items.ex: Por supuesto, pueden contar conmigo para organizar el evento.
items.exEn: Of course, you can count on me to organize the event.

items.use: THE key contrast connector for writing. Starts a new sentence or follows a semicolon, with a comma after it: "…; sin embargo, …". Use it in every opinion essay.
items.ex: La ciudad tiene buenos parques. Sin embargo, faltan ciclovías.
items.exEn: The city has good parks. However, it lacks bike lanes.

items.use: Explains or clarifies the previous idea. Commas around it. Neutral to formal: the written version of "o sea".
items.ex: El curso es intensivo, es decir, tiene clases todos los días.
items.exEn: The course is intensive, that is, it has classes every day.

items.use: A slightly more formal "porque"; it can go at the start or in the middle. Very good in essays and formal emails.
items.ex: Le escribo ya que no he recibido respuesta a mi reclamo.
items.exEn: I'm writing to you since I haven't received a reply to my complaint.

items.use: Brings in a side topic. Informal to neutral; perfect in a friendly email or conversation, not in an essay.
items.ex: Nos vemos el viernes. Por cierto, ¿ya compraste las entradas?
items.exEn: See you Friday. By the way, did you already buy the tickets?

items.use: Compares two different things or people. Comma after it at the start. Good in essays and when comparing photos in the oral test.
items.ex: Mi hermano odia el calor. Yo, en cambio, no podría vivir sin playa.
items.exEn: My brother hates the heat. I, on the other hand, couldn't live without the beach.

items.use: Keeps your point even after a problem or objection. Comma after it. Neutral: emails, speaking, and informal essays.
items.ex: No sé si llegue a tiempo. De todas formas, te aviso.
items.exEn: I don't know if I'll make it on time. Anyway, I'll let you know.

items.use: Same as "de todas formas"; switch between them to avoid repetition. Comma after it at the start.
items.ex: Quizás el museo esté cerrado; de todos modos, vamos a intentarlo.
items.exEn: Maybe the museum is closed; anyway, let's give it a try.

items.use: Third version of "anyway", very common in Latin America. Use it in speech and emails.
items.ex: Ya cené, pero de todas maneras te acompaño al restaurante.
items.exEn: I already had dinner, but I'll come with you to the restaurant anyway.
items.latam: Very frequent in Panama; Spain tends to prefer "de todas formas".

items.use: Spoken way to sum up a story, often with a hint of frustration: "Total, que…". Speaking only.
items.ex: El vuelo se retrasó y perdí la conexión. Total, llegué un día después.
items.exEn: The flight was delayed and I missed my connection. Long story short, I arrived a day late.

items.use: Closes a topic or story, sometimes with resignation. Spoken and informal emails. Comma after it.
items.ex: Perdí el celular y las llaves. En fin, mañana será otro día.
items.exEn: I lost my cell phone and my keys. Oh well, tomorrow is another day.

items.use: The simplest way to give an opinion; it takes the indicative. Negative "no creo que" takes the subjunctive. Use it in every oral task.
items.ex: El problema es grave. Creo que el gobierno debe hacer algo pronto.
items.exEn: The problem is serious. I think the government should do something soon.

items.use: Short spoken way to give your opinion. Comma after it at the start. Good in speaking; in essays prefer "en mi opinión".
items.ex: Para mí, lo más importante de un trabajo es el ambiente.
items.exEn: For me, the most important thing about a job is the atmosphere.

items.use: Clear opinion marker for essays and the oral monologue. Comma after it. Then use indicative: "En mi opinión, es…".
items.ex: Hay varias propuestas. En mi opinión, la más realista es la segunda.
items.exEn: There are several proposals. In my opinion, the most realistic is the second one.

items.use: Sets a minimum or finds something positive in a bad situation. Neutral: works in all tasks.
items.ex: El hotel era viejo, pero por lo menos estaba limpio.
items.exEn: The hotel was old, but at least it was clean.

items.use: Same as "por lo menos", slightly more written. Use both to vary your text.
items.ex: No ganamos el partido; al menos jugamos bien.
items.exEn: We didn't win the game; at least we played well.

items.use: Latin American spoken filler while you look for a word: "Este… no sé." One or two in the oral test sound natural; too many sound nervous.
items.ex: Me gustaría trabajar en, este… algo relacionado con el turismo.
items.exEn: I'd like to work in, um… something related to tourism.
items.latam: Typical of Panama and Latin America; Spain uses "esto" or "eh" instead.

items.use: Spoken softener before an approximate or careful word. Useful in the oral test to rephrase gently.
items.ex: No es que sea malo; es, digamos, un poco desorganizado.
items.exEn: It's not that he's bad; he's, let's say, a bit disorganized.

items.use: Adds one more negative point, usually in complaints. Informal: great in speech and a complaint email to a friend, not in a formal essay.
items.ex: El servicio fue lento y, encima, la comida llegó fría.
items.exEn: The service was slow and, on top of that, the food arrived cold.

items.use: Keeps your conclusion despite the problem you just mentioned. Note: "aun" without accent here. Good in essays and speaking.
items.ex: El alquiler es caro. Aun así, prefiero vivir cerca de la oficina.
items.exEn: The rent is expensive. Even so, I prefer to live near the office.

items.use: Formal-neutral result connector for essays and formal emails. Comma after it: "Por lo tanto, …". The upgrade of "entonces".
items.ex: El transporte público no es suficiente. Por lo tanto, la gente usa el carro.
items.exEn: Public transport isn't enough. Therefore, people use their cars.

items.use: Contrasts two facts in one sentence, with a comma before it. Very useful for comparing photos or data in the DELE.
items.ex: En la ciudad hace calor, mientras que en Boquete hace fresco.
items.exEn: In the city it's hot, whereas in Boquete it's cool.

items.use: Informal "incluso" before a surprising case. Common in speech; in essays use "incluso".
items.ex: Todos bailaron en la boda; hasta mi abuela se levantó.
items.exEn: Everyone danced at the wedding; even my grandma got up.

items.use: Negative emphasis. Before the verb it needs no "no": "Ni siquiera llamó." After the verb: "No llamó ni siquiera una vez."
items.ex: Estaba tan cansado que ni siquiera cené.
items.exEn: I was so tired that I didn't even have dinner.

items.use: Gives an overall view before or after details. Neutral; good in essays and to open the oral monologue.
items.ex: Hubo algunos problemas, pero en general el viaje salió bien.
items.exEn: There were some problems, but in general the trip went well.

items.use: Describes what normally happens. Neutral; useful in emails describing your routine.
items.ex: Trabajo desde casa. Por lo general, empiezo a las ocho.
items.exEn: I work from home. Usually I start at eight.

items.use: Highlights one part of a group. Formal-neutral; slightly more written than "sobre todo".
items.ex: El tráfico es terrible, especialmente en la hora pico.
items.exEn: The traffic is terrible, especially at rush hour.

items.use: Describes how things were at the start, often before a change ("pero luego…"). Great for narrating experiences in emails.
items.ex: Al principio no entendía nada, pero después me acostumbré.
items.exEn: At first I didn't understand anything, but later I got used to it.

items.use: Shows relief after waiting. Not for listing points; use "por último" for that.
items.ex: Después de tres meses buscando, por fin encontré apartamento.
items.exEn: After three months of searching, I finally found an apartment.

items.use: Introduces the last point or the last step. Comma after it. Good to close an argument list in an essay.
items.ex: Hablé de las ventajas y los riesgos. Finalmente, daré mi opinión.
items.exEn: I talked about the advantages and risks. Finally, I'll give my opinion.

items.use: Shows two things happening at the same time. Comma after it at the start. Good for narrating.
items.ex: Yo preparo la cena. Mientras tanto, tú pones la mesa.
items.exEn: I'll make dinner. Meanwhile, you set the table.

items.use: Swaps one option for another; followed by a noun or infinitive. Useful when proposing alternatives in essays.
items.ex: En vez de quejarnos, deberíamos buscar soluciones.
items.exEn: Instead of complaining, we should look for solutions.

items.use: Same as "en vez de", slightly more formal. Use both to avoid repeating.
items.ex: Propongo usar el bus en lugar del carro para ir al centro.
items.exEn: I suggest using the bus instead of the car to go downtown.

items.use: Followed by a noun or infinitive ("a pesar de la lluvia"), or "a pesar de que" + verb. Strong essay connector for concession.
items.ex: A pesar de la lluvia, mucha gente fue al desfile.
items.exEn: Despite the rain, lots of people went to the parade.

items.use: Opens the first side of an argument; must be followed later by "por otro (lado)". Perfect for the body of an opinion essay.
items.ex: Por un lado, el teletrabajo ahorra tiempo de transporte.
items.exEn: On one hand, remote work saves commuting time.

items.use: Gives the second side after "por un lado", or simply adds another point. Comma after it.
items.ex: Por otro lado, muchas personas se sienten solas trabajando en casa.
items.exEn: On the other hand, many people feel lonely working from home.

items.use: Formal way to start a list of arguments. Comma after it. Use it in essays and the monologue to sound organized.
items.ex: En primer lugar, quisiera agradecerles la invitación.
items.exEn: First of all, I'd like to thank you for the invitation.

items.use: Continues a list after "en primer lugar". Then "en tercer lugar" or "por último".
items.ex: En segundo lugar, el proyecto es demasiado caro para la comunidad.
items.exEn: Secondly, the project is too expensive for the community.

items.use: Introduces the last item of a list. Comma after it. Classic essay and monologue connector.
items.ex: Por último, me gustaría hablar de las soluciones posibles.
items.exEn: Lastly, I'd like to talk about possible solutions.

items.use: Opens a talk or list in a friendly, clear way. Very good for starting the oral monologue.
items.ex: Para empezar, les cuento por qué elegí este tema.
items.exEn: To begin with, I'll tell you why I chose this topic.

items.use: Signals that you're closing. Comma after it. Great in the oral monologue and at the end of an email.
items.ex: Para terminar, quiero repetir que la idea me parece excelente.
items.exEn: To finish, I want to repeat that I think the idea is excellent.

items.use: Formal-neutral opinion opener; comma after it. Use it to vary "en mi opinión" in essays.
items.ex: Desde mi punto de vista, la educación debería ser más práctica.
items.exEn: From my point of view, education should be more practical.

items.use: Elegant opinion marker, good for B2 essays and monologues. Comma after it.
items.ex: A mi modo de ver, el problema no es el dinero sino la organización.
items.exEn: The way I see it, the problem isn't money but organization.

items.use: Marks your own view, often after presenting others'. Comma after it at the start.
items.ex: Muchos prefieren la playa. Personalmente, prefiero la montaña.
items.exEn: Many people prefer the beach. Personally, I prefer the mountains.

items.use: Cites a source or someone's opinion: "según el texto", "según yo" (informal). Very useful when you discuss data in the DELE.
items.ex: Según el estudio, los jóvenes leen más en el celular que en papel.
items.exEn: According to the study, young people read more on their phones than on paper.

items.use: Reports something you heard or deduced, without fully confirming it. Neutral; good in emails and speaking.
items.ex: Por lo visto, van a cerrar la calle por las obras del metro.
items.exEn: Apparently, they're going to close the street for the metro works.

items.use: Like "por lo visto" but a little more formal; common in news. Comma after it.
items.ex: Al parecer, el concierto se canceló por la lluvia.
items.exEn: Apparently, the concert was canceled because of the rain.

items.use: Marks something as clear to everyone. Neutral; don't overuse it in essays or it sounds arrogant.
items.ex: Obviamente, nadie quiere pagar más impuestos.
items.exEn: Obviously, nobody wants to pay more taxes.

items.use: More formal "obviamente"; good in essays. Comma after it at the start.
items.ex: Evidentemente, la situación no puede seguir así.
items.exEn: Clearly, the situation can't go on like this.

items.use: Strong agreement or emphasis; slightly more elegant than "claro". Good in speaking and formal emails.
items.ex: Desde luego, estoy dispuesto a trabajar los fines de semana.
items.exEn: Certainly, I'm willing to work on weekends.

items.use: "Claro que sí / no" or "claro que + sentence" stresses that something is obvious. Spoken; also can concede: "Claro que es caro, pero…".
items.ex: Claro que es caro, pero la calidad lo vale.
items.exEn: Of course it's expensive, but the quality is worth it.

items.use: Strongly confirms your view. Neutral to formal; nice in essay conclusions.
items.ex: Sin duda, fue la mejor experiencia de mi vida.
items.exEn: Without a doubt, it was the best experience of my life.

items.use: Adds a small condition or warning after a positive idea. Spoken and informal emails; very natural.
items.ex: Puedes usar mi carro; eso sí, devuélvelo con gasolina.
items.exEn: You can use my car; mind you, bring it back with gas.

items.use: Corrects or makes your description more exact. Neutral; useful in speaking when you rephrase.
items.ex: No es tímido; es más bien reservado.
items.exEn: He's not shy; he's more reserved, rather.

items.use: Use after a negative to replace the wrong idea: "no A sino B". English speakers often wrongly use "pero" here.
items.ex: El problema no es el precio sino la calidad.
items.exEn: The problem isn't the price but the quality.

items.use: Adds a second, stronger point in one sentence. Excellent in essays to sound advanced.
items.ex: El deporte no solo mejora la salud, sino también el ánimo.
items.exEn: Sport not only improves health but also mood.

items.use: Joins two elements equally: "tanto los niños como los adultos". Formal-neutral; good in essays.
items.ex: Tanto los estudiantes como los profesores apoyan el cambio.
items.exEn: Both the students and the teachers support the change.

items.use: Adds another point after mentioning one. Neutral, a bit spoken. In formal writing use "asimismo".
items.ex: El hotel tenía piscina. Aparte de eso, el desayuno era excelente.
items.exEn: The hotel had a pool. Apart from that, the breakfast was excellent.

items.use: Followed by a noun or infinitive: "además de estudiar, trabajo". Avoids repeating "y".
items.ex: Además de ser barato, el mercado tiene productos muy frescos.
items.exEn: Besides being cheap, the market has very fresh produce.

items.use: Formal way to add an element to a list. Good in essays and formal letters.
items.ex: Se necesitan más médicos, así como mejores hospitales.
items.exEn: More doctors are needed, as well as better hospitals.

items.use: Formal cause + noun: "debido al tráfico". Common in formal emails and news. "Debido a que" + verb.
items.ex: El vuelo salió tarde debido al mal tiempo.
items.exEn: The flight left late due to bad weather.

items.use: Positive cause + noun or person. Use "por culpa de" for negative causes.
items.ex: Gracias a la beca, pude estudiar en el extranjero.
items.exEn: Thanks to the scholarship, I was able to study abroad.

items.use: Negative cause; puts the blame on something. Informal-neutral; good in complaint emails.
items.ex: Perdimos el bus por culpa del tranque.
items.exEn: We missed the bus because of the traffic jam.
items.latam: "Tranque" is the Panamanian word for a traffic jam; Spain says "atasco".

items.use: Neutral-formal cause + noun. A good way to vary "debido a".
items.ex: Muchas cosechas se perdieron a causa de la sequía.
items.exEn: Many crops were lost because of the drought.

items.use: Formal "ya que"; can open a sentence. Very good in essays and formal letters.
items.ex: Puesto que nadie se opuso, aprobamos la propuesta.
items.exEn: Since nobody objected, we approved the proposal.

items.use: Formal cause, usually at the start of the sentence. Great for arguments in essays.
items.ex: Dado que los precios suben, la gente gasta menos.
items.exEn: Given that prices are rising, people spend less.

items.use: Points back clearly to the reason just stated. Comma after it. Clear and neutral for essays.
items.ex: Muchas familias viven lejos. Por esta razón, necesitan buen transporte.
items.exEn: Many families live far away. For this reason, they need good transport.

items.use: Introduces a result (indicative) or a purpose (subjunctive). Neutral-formal; good in essays.
items.ex: No había mesas libres, de modo que comimos en la barra.
items.exEn: There were no free tables, so we ate at the bar.

items.en: so, in such a way that
items.use: Same as "de modo que"; use both to vary. Result = indicative, purpose = subjunctive.
items.ex: Hablé despacio, de manera que todos me entendieran.
items.exEn: I spoke slowly so that everyone would understand me.

items.use: Links a result to the whole previous idea. Common in speech and semi-formal writing.
items.ex: Cerraron la biblioteca, con lo cual tuve que estudiar en casa.
items.exEn: They closed the library, which meant I had to study at home.

items.use: Formal result connector for essays and reports. Comma after it.
items.ex: La empresa perdió clientes. En consecuencia, redujo personal.
items.exEn: The company lost customers. Consequently, it cut staff.

items.use: Very formal result connector: the written pair of "por eso". Use it once per essay to show range.
items.ex: El plazo ya venció; por consiguiente, no podemos aceptar su solicitud.
items.exEn: The deadline has passed; consequently, we can't accept your application.

items.use: Formal version of "por lo tanto". Common in academic writing. Comma after it.
items.ex: Los datos son incompletos; por tanto, el estudio no es concluyente.
items.exEn: The data are incomplete; therefore, the study isn't conclusive.

items.use: Formal: draws a conclusion from what came before. Comma after it. Good to open the final paragraph of an essay.
items.ex: Todos los expertos coinciden. Así pues, es hora de actuar.
items.exEn: All the experts agree. So, it's time to act.

items.use: Formal consequence that takes the SUBJUNCTIVE: "de ahí que haya…". A strong C1 marker in essays.
items.ex: El alquiler es carísimo; de ahí que muchos jóvenes vivan con sus padres.
items.exEn: Rent is very expensive; hence many young people live with their parents.

items.use: Opens a summary of what you said. Comma after it. Use it in the last paragraph of an essay or end of the monologue.
items.ex: En resumen, la propuesta tiene más ventajas que desventajas.
items.exEn: In short, the proposal has more advantages than disadvantages.

items.use: Spoken-neutral summary marker, good at the end of the oral monologue.
items.ex: Resumiendo, necesitamos más tiempo y más presupuesto.
items.exEn: Summing up, we need more time and a bigger budget.

items.use: The classic essay closer. Comma after it, then restate your opinion briefly. Don't add new arguments after it.
items.ex: En conclusión, creo que las redes sociales hacen más bien que mal.
items.exEn: In conclusion, I think social media does more good than harm.

items.use: Alternative to "en conclusión"; good in essays and the oral monologue.
items.ex: Para concluir, les agradezco su atención.
items.exEn: To conclude, thank you for your attention.

items.use: Gives the final, essential conclusion. Formal-neutral; strong at B2 and C1.
items.ex: En definitiva, el éxito depende del esfuerzo de todos.
items.exEn: Ultimately, success depends on everyone's effort.

items.use: Formal written closer for essays and reports. Comma after it.
items.ex: A modo de conclusión, propongo tres medidas concretas.
items.exEn: By way of conclusion, I propose three concrete measures.

items.en: after all, at the end of the day
items.use: Gives the final, decisive reason. Neutral; works well in speaking and essays.
items.ex: No te preocupes por el error; al fin y al cabo, todos nos equivocamos.
items.exEn: Don't worry about the mistake; after all, we all make mistakes.

items.en: when all is said and done
items.use: Like "al fin y al cabo": the bottom-line reason. Comma after it.
items.ex: Es mejor pagar un poco más; a fin de cuentas, es tu salud.
items.exEn: It's better to pay a bit more; when all is said and done, it's your health.

items.use: Reminds of a key fact that justifies your view. Neutral; good in speaking.
items.ex: Perdónalo; después de todo, es tu hermano.
items.exEn: Forgive him; after all, he's your brother.

items.use: Moves from a point you accept to your main view. Elegant in essays and debates; comma after it.
items.ex: El plan tiene fallos. Dicho esto, es mejor que no hacer nada.
items.exEn: The plan has flaws. Having said that, it's better than doing nothing.

items.use: Formal pair of "pero"/"sin embargo". Comma after it. Perfect for formal letters and essays.
items.ex: Su currículum es excelente. No obstante, buscamos a alguien con más experiencia.
items.exEn: Your résumé is excellent. However, we're looking for someone with more experience.

items.use: Introduces an important objection or condition. Formal-neutral; strong in essays and debates.
items.ex: La idea es buena. Ahora bien, ¿quién la va a pagar?
items.exEn: The idea is good. Now, who's going to pay for it?

items.use: Presents the opposite of what was just said. Comma after it. Good in essays.
items.ex: El cambio no perjudica a los clientes; por el contrario, los beneficia.
items.exEn: The change doesn't hurt customers; on the contrary, it benefits them.

items.use: Same as "por el contrario", a bit more spoken. Also as a reply: "¡Al contrario!"
items.ex: No me molesta que vengas; al contrario, me alegra mucho.
items.exEn: I don't mind you coming; on the contrary, I'm really glad.

items.use: Compares two things + noun. Very useful in the DELE photo or data comparison.
items.ex: A diferencia de la capital, en el interior la vida es más tranquila.
items.exEn: Unlike the capital, life in the countryside is calmer.
items.latam: In Panama "el interior" means the provinces outside Panama City.

items.use: Formal "aunque" with indicative: admits a point before your main idea. Strong C1 essay marker.
items.ex: Si bien la ley es necesaria, su aplicación será difícil.
items.exEn: Although the law is necessary, applying it will be difficult.

items.use: Formal "a pesar de" + noun or infinitive. Common in news and formal essays.
items.ex: Pese a las críticas, el alcalde mantuvo el proyecto.
items.exEn: Despite the criticism, the mayor kept the project.

items.use: Formal concession after listing problems. Comma after it. Rare in speech, elegant in essays.
items.ex: El sistema tiene muchos defectos. Con todo, es el mejor que tenemos.
items.exEn: The system has many flaws. Even so, it's the best we have.

items.en: in any case, at any rate
items.use: Keeps a point valid whatever happens, or limits what you said. Neutral-formal.
items.ex: Puede que llueva. En todo caso, llevaremos paraguas.
items.exEn: It may rain. In any case, we'll take umbrellas.

items.use: Same as "en todo caso"; good in formal emails to move to a practical point.
items.ex: No sé si podré asistir. En cualquier caso, le confirmaré el lunes.
items.exEn: I don't know if I'll be able to attend. In any case, I'll confirm on Monday.

items.use: Formal pair of "además"/"también". One word. Comma after it. Ideal for formal letters and essays.
items.ex: Solicito información sobre el curso. Asimismo, quisiera conocer los precios.
items.exEn: I'm requesting information about the course. Likewise, I'd like to know the prices.

items.use: Adds a similar point in formal writing. In speech it also means "same to you".
items.ex: Es importante ahorrar. Igualmente, conviene evitar las deudas.
items.exEn: It's important to save. Likewise, it's wise to avoid debt.

items.use: Shows that a second idea works like the first. Formal; comma after it.
items.ex: Las empresas deben reciclar. Del mismo modo, los ciudadanos deben hacerlo en casa.
items.exEn: Companies should recycle. Similarly, citizens should do it at home.

items.use: Shows a chain of effects or a parallel action. Formal; good in essays explaining causes.
items.ex: El desempleo reduce el consumo, lo que a su vez afecta a los negocios.
items.exEn: Unemployment reduces spending, which in turn affects businesses.

items.use: Adds a stronger point that pushes your argument further. Comma after it. Common in speech and essays.
items.ex: No me parece caro. Es más, creo que es una ganga.
items.exEn: I don't think it's expensive. What's more, I think it's a bargain.

items.use: Adds the last and worst problem. Informal; great when telling a bad experience in speech or a friendly email.
items.ex: Llovió todo el día y, para colmo, se fue la luz.
items.exEn: It rained all day and, to top it all off, the power went out.

items.use: Adds one more strong point (good or bad). Expressive; works in speech and lively essays.
items.ex: El hotel es precioso y, por si fuera poco, está frente al mar.
items.exEn: The hotel is gorgeous and, as if that weren't enough, it's on the beach.

items.use: Corrects what you just said. Comma before and after. Great in the oral test when you make a slip.
items.ex: Nos vemos el lunes, mejor dicho, el martes.
items.exEn: See you Monday, or rather, Tuesday.

items.use: Restates a complex idea more simply. Neutral-formal; good in essays.
items.ex: La empresa va a reestructurarse; en otras palabras, habrá despidos.
items.exEn: The company is going to restructure; in other words, there will be layoffs.

items.use: Formal reformulation; use it to vary "es decir" in essays.
items.ex: Los recursos son limitados. Dicho de otro modo, hay que elegir prioridades.
items.exEn: Resources are limited. Put another way, we have to choose priorities.

items.w: o lo que es lo mismo
items.en: or, to put it another way
items.use: Restates the idea in clearer or blunter terms. Formal-neutral; gives an essay a C1 touch.
items.ex: Ganan el salario mínimo, o lo que es lo mismo, apenas llegan a fin de mes.
items.exEn: They earn minimum wage, or to put it another way, they barely make ends meet.

items.use: Narrows a general idea to a specific case. Neutral; useful in emails and essays.
items.ex: Tengo un problema con la factura; en concreto, con el último cargo.
items.exEn: I have a problem with the bill; specifically, with the last charge.

items.use: Points to one specific example within a group. Neutral-formal.
items.ex: Me gustan los deportes acuáticos, en particular el surf.
items.exEn: I like water sports, in particular surfing.

items.use: Introduces a new topic or aspect. Excellent for organizing paragraphs in essays and emails.
items.ex: En cuanto al precio, creo que es razonable.
items.exEn: As for the price, I think it's reasonable.

items.use: Formal topic marker; also "respecto a". Very common in formal emails: "Con respecto a su consulta…".
items.ex: Con respecto a su consulta, le informamos que el curso empieza en enero.
items.exEn: Regarding your inquiry, we inform you that the course starts in January.

items.w: en lo que se refiere a
items.use: Formal, longer topic marker; nice for starting a paragraph in a C1-level essay.
items.ex: En lo que se refiere a la salud, los resultados son positivos.
items.exEn: As far as health is concerned, the results are positive.

items.use: Formal topic marker for letters and reports. ("En relación a" is also heard but less recommended.)
items.ex: Le escribo en relación con el anuncio publicado ayer.
items.exEn: I'm writing to you regarding the ad published yesterday.

items.use: Announces what comes next in a text or talk. Formal-neutral; great in the oral monologue and reports.
items.ex: A continuación, voy a explicar las dos opciones.
items.exEn: Next, I'm going to explain the two options.

items.use: Starts with the most basic or polite point. Good to open an email or a talk.
items.ex: Antes que nada, muchas gracias por su ayuda.
items.exEn: First of all, thank you very much for your help.

items.use: Marks the top priority. Formal-neutral; good in essays and speeches.
items.ex: Ante todo, hay que garantizar la seguridad de los niños.
items.exEn: Above all, we must guarantee the children's safety.

items.use: Formal version of "por un lado"; pair it with "por otra parte". Good for structured essays.
items.ex: Por una parte, el turismo genera empleo.
items.exEn: On the one hand, tourism creates jobs.

items.use: Gives the other side or adds a new point. Formal; comma after it.
items.ex: Por otra parte, puede dañar el medio ambiente.
items.exEn: On the other hand, it can damage the environment.

items.use: Formal opinion marker; sounds mature in essays and debates. Comma after it.
items.ex: A mi juicio, la medida llega demasiado tarde.
items.exEn: In my judgment, the measure comes too late.

items.use: Formal written phrase to stress an important fact. Great in essays and reports; too stiff for conversation.
items.ex: Las ventas subieron. Cabe destacar que fue el mejor año de la década.
items.exEn: Sales went up. It's worth highlighting that it was the best year of the decade.

items.w: hay que tener en cuenta que
items.en: we must bear in mind that
items.use: Introduces an important factor before deciding. Neutral; very useful in essays and the oral negotiation task.
items.ex: La idea es buena, pero hay que tener en cuenta que el presupuesto es bajo.
items.exEn: The idea is good, but we must bear in mind that the budget is low.

items.use: Formally confirms what was said or expected. Written and formal speech.
items.ex: Se esperaba una mejora y, en efecto, los resultados subieron.
items.exEn: An improvement was expected and, indeed, the results went up.

items.use: Confirms something. In speech it's a strong "yes, exactly"; in writing, formal confirmation.
items.ex: —¿Usted llamó ayer? —Efectivamente, llamé por lo del contrato.
items.exEn: "Did you call yesterday?" "Yes, indeed, I called about the contract."

items.use: Goes to the real, hidden nature of something. Neutral; good in speaking and essays.
items.ex: Parece serio, pero en el fondo es muy bromista.
items.exEn: He seems serious, but deep down he's a big joker.
